original_draft: Mount Everest, on the border between Nepal and the Tibet Autonomous Region of China, is the highest mountain above sea level. In 2020, China and Nepal jointly announced a height of 8,848.86 metres. The mountain is part of the Mahalangur Himal section of the Himalayas. Edmund Hillary of New Zealand and the Sherpa mountaineer Tenzing Norgay made the first confirmed ascent on May 29, 1953, as members of a British expedition led by John Hunt. The most common route from Nepal climbs through the Rongbuk Glacier and reaches the summit by the southeast ridge.

The most common route from Nepal climbs through the Khumbu Icefall and reaches the summit by the southeast ridge.
